subject: Deployment mode follow-up & migration qualification - Nova Health

Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode options & migration checklist

Hi Sarah
- great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

Summary of needs:
- Primary goal: replace current self-hosted inference pipeline (on-prem GPU cluster) with a managed solution to reduce ops burden while meeting HIPAA/PHI controls.
- Key constraints: data residency in US, SOC2 evidence, customer-managed KMS preferred for sensitive workflows, procurement window ~Q3.
- Performance: expect ~150 concurrent requests at peak, 75 reqs/s sustained, target p95 latency < 250ms for short-chat flows.

Deployment modes we discussed:
1) Hosted API
- fastest to get started, lowest operational overhead, Redwood-managed keys and infrastructure. Good for pilot and non-PII traffic.
2) Dedicated capacity
- reserved GPU pools, single-tenant performance with predictable throughput. Allows custom autoscaling and some network restrictions.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem)
- full private control plane, supports air-gapped or on-prem install for regulated workloads, integrates with customer KMS/HSM.

From our conversation it sounds like Nova Health is leaning toward Dedicated or Private because of compliance + existing on-prem investment. To help you evaluate quickly I attached our Dedicated pricing sheet and a mutual action plan with suggested milestones.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm which workloads will be in-scope for the pilot (PHI vs non-PHI)?
- Please share basic infra details for the on-prem cluster (GPU types, network topology, egress rules) if you want a migration plan for model weights/KV cache.
- I'll loop in Neha (solutions) and Lukas (sales engineer) for a technical deep-dive next week.

Proposed times: Tue 6/8 or Wed 6/9 between 10 PT. What works best?

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Thanks

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa
- thanks for the recap, that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from procurement/infra:

- Pilot scope: start with non-PII customer support transcripts (chatbot) and then expand to PHI workflows if Dedicated or Private meets our controls.
- Current infra: on-prem GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100s, Kubernetes) behind a corporate firewall. We do nightly incremental model snapshot backups to S3-compatible storage.
- Compliance: SOC 2 type II report required for vendor assessment; KMS integration is preferred (we can provide key provisioning details).
- Timeline: procurement approval earliest mid-August; evaluation + technical pilot ideally complete by end of Q3.

We're definitely more comfortable with Dedicated or Private depending on the level of KMS control and egress protections. Would a short Dedicated pilot with strict network ACLs and customer KMS be a supported path?

Thanks Sarah
- yes, Dedicated with customer KMS is a supported path and is a common migration route for customers moving from a hosted LLM API or self-hosted GPU clusters. A few notes to address your migration questions:

Migration considerations:
- From another LLM API: main tasks are prompt/response normalization, rate-limit and batching behavior changes, and verifying tokenization differences. We typically recommend a short shadowing period (2 weeks) where requests are proxied through Redwood for side-by-side output comparison.
- From self-hosted cluster: you'll want to export model artifacts and any custom tokenizer configs; KV cache warmup strategy is important (we can snapshot chat contexts to prime caches). Network egress and firewall rules must allow connections to the Dedicated pool endpoints or set up a Private VPC peering if you choose Private.

Technical deep-dive agenda (30-45 min):
- Infra topology & network requirements (firewall rules, VPN/peering options)
- KMS/HSM integration and key rotation flows
- Performance targets (concurrency, latency expectations) and autoscaling behavior
- Migration runbook and rollback plan

I've attached a mutual action plan with proposed milestones. Proposed times still Tue 6/8 10am PT or Wed 6/9 11am PT. I'll block both tentatively.
